game.name: Ai Senshi Nicol
game.desc: Ajude o inventor corajoso Nicol resgatar sua namorada raptada Stella de um Demon Bull King do planeta Dairass neste jogo de ação suspensa. Controle Nicol através de 7 continentes como ele recupera 3 peças em cada nível a sua invenção de transportador dimensional que o Demon King roubou e envolto em diamantes. Você vai explodir em vários asseclas e evitar terreno traiçoeiro ao explorar vários andares de cada continente procurando os diamantes para ser re-unido com Stella e derrotar o malvado Demon King!

game.name: Aki to Tsukasa no Fushigi no Kabe
game.desc: Um jogo hentai sem licença que é basicamente tênis de mesa solo onde você bateu certas partes de uma parede para revelar uma menina em uma pose erótica.

game.name: Akumajou Dracula
game.desc: Akumajō Dracula (also known as Castlevania) is a 1986 Famicom Disk System side-scrolling horror action platformer video game developed and released by Konami in Japan on September 26, 1986. Transylvania enjoyed a century of peace thanks to the legendary hero, Christopher Belmont, a vampire hunter who vanquished Count Dracula one hundred years earlier with a holy whip named Vampire Killer. While the Easter celebration carried on with a grand carnival, evil men gathered in a monastery at the edge of the village and conducted a black mass to resurrect Count Dracula. The men succeeded in bringing their master back. A bolt of lightning enveloped the monastery where they held the rite, signaling the resurrection of Count Dracula. When the Count returned, his Castle, which had fallen one hundred years prior, reappeared in Transylvania, and his legions of loyal minions reformed. Simon Belmont, the descendant of Christopher Belmont, knew that as a member of the Belmont Clan and the current wielder of the Vampire Killer whip, it was his duty to bring peace and stability back to Transylvania by destroying Dracula.

game.name: Akuu Senki Raijin
game.desc: A scrolling mecha shooter published by Squaresoft for the Famicom Disk System. Akuu Senki Raijin (occasionally transliterated as Akara Senki Raijin) is a vertical shooter where the player controls a mecha that transforms into a starfighter. The game was published by Squaresoft, via their DOG label for Famicom Disk System games, and developed by Micro Cabin. Akuu Senki Raijin (and Moonball Magic, released the same day) would be the last DOG game published - Square would exclusively focus on the regular cart-based Famicom from then on. Like Square's earlier semi-classic Thexder, the player can opt to change between the two modes of their craft at certain points during each level. Upon touching ground as the mecha, the player is occasionally able to find other directions to continue exploring as a spaceship, presenting both vertical-scrolling and side-scrolling shoot-'em-up sections.

game.name: All Night Nippon Super Mario Brothers
game.desc: An officially licensed retool of Super Mario Bros., released in 1986 for the Famicom Disk System. This version is based on the Japanese radio program All Night Nippon, and it was given out as a raffle prize on the show itself. The game was published by Fuji Television. Essentially, this game is an exact replica of the original, except with the sprites of the Toads and various enemies replaced with Japanese celebrities for a humorous effect.

game.name: Apple Town Monogatari - Little Computer People
game.desc: A version of Little Computer People for Nintendo's Family Computer Disk System version, published in Japan by DOG (a subsidiary of Square). Based on the original game by Activision. Unlike previous versions of Little Computer People, the playable character is a girl wearing a pink dress and bow in her hair. The rooms of the house are also in a different configuration, featuring an outdoor balcony on the top floor. When the game is first played, a name for the character is chosen at random from a preprogrammed list. There are no winning conditions on this game you basically watch and interact with the girl in various ways. However, Apple Town Story lacks many of the features found in other versions of Little Computer People.

game.name: Armana no Kiseki
game.desc: Uma jóia vermelha mágica conhecida como Almana é roubada de uma aldeia sem nome. Um ladrão foge com a jóia e transforma toda a aldeia em pedra. O jogador assume o papel de Kaito um herói que se assemelha a Indiana Jones e deve viajar através de seis níveis cavernosos em busca da jóia perdida. A principal fonte de transporte de Kaito é única. Além de apenas andar e saltar, como a maioria dos jogos de plataforma, ele também deve usar um gancho de grappling especial para alcançar plataformas que são muito altas. Para tornar as coisas um pouco mais difíceis, o gancho de garra só pode ser lançado de uma direção diagonal e não apenas diretamente acima.

game.name: Big Challenge! Juudou Senshuken
game.desc: Grande Desafio! Judo Senshuken (lit. Big Challenge! Judo Championship) é um jogo de competição desportiva com temática judaica desenvolvido para o Famicom Disk System e publicado pela Jaleco Entertainment em 1988. É o primeiro título da série "Big Challenge!" da Jaleco. O objetivo do jogo é derrotar o adversário usando movimentos legais de judô. Isso envolve um monte de grapples, pinos e lançamentos. Derrotar um adversário permite que o jogador para trabalhar sua maneira acima das fileiras do torneio para os inimigos progressivamente mais difíceis.

game.name: Bio Miracle Bokutte Upa
game.desc: Upa is the prince of a magical kingdom and the most recent in a line of brave fighters. One day, though, he broke an urn containing the spirit of Zai, an incredibly evil goatish demon who takes the life force of the kingdom's adults and kidnaps all the babies - except for Upa, who is given a magical rattle by a fairy who was trapped in the urn along with Zai. And so, in order to save his kingdom, Upa crawls into action... He will navigating side scrolling stages with platforms and can inflate enemies by hitting them with his rattle for use as temporary platforms or to throw at adversaries.

Cocona World
game.desc: You control a young witch who wanders throughout various parts of the kingdom. There are many animal inhabitants to interact with, some of which are good and some of which are evil. There are also a number of activities to perform and mini-games to play. Over time, the witch will request that certain activities be performed. If they are not performed within a certain time period, the player receives a penalty. Over time, the character's mood and strength will drop. If both of these are never restored and drop to zero, the game is over. This game was only released in Japan, and has never been translated into English.

Adian no Tsue
game.desc: Adian No Tsue não é um jogo de aventura tradicional - É, acima de tudo, um jogo educativo concebido para atrair um público jovem. É também a primeira parcela de uma série de jogos lançados no Japão pela SunSoft. O jogador assume o controle de um corajoso cavaleiro e o jogo segue uma tradicional exibição aérea que, de alguma forma, tem alguma semelhança com Zelda da Nintendo. Cada quarto é geralmente preenchido com monstros e quatro portas levam a outras salas circundantes, locais diferentes ou apenas esconder itens especiais. Contudo, a única forma de o nosso herói passar por estas portas é resolver equações aritméticas simples. Números de 0 a 9 aparecem em dois lados da sala e o cavaleiro deve correr pela sala e tocá-los para mostrar a resposta certa. No entanto, estas expressões são muito simples e usam apenas simples adições, subtracções, multiplicações e divisões. No entanto, resolvê-las enquanto correm pelas salas e atingem esqueletos loucos com uma espada pode ser uma tarefa desafiadora. O outro lado do disco contém um simples jogo de maratona também baseado em desafios aritméticos.
